story_type: rocket cam over the California coast, sea level satellite
hook: A camera on this rocket watched the launch pad fall away.
narration: A camera on this rocket looked straight down at the launch pad as it climbed away.
It lifted off from Vandenberg Air Force Base on November twenty-first, 2020.
On top was Sentinel-6, a satellite that measures rising seas.
About a minute in, the rocket went supersonic, then flew through maximum aerodynamic pressure.
Max Q is the moment when speed and air density squeeze the rocket hardest, so the engines ease back to get through it.
[short pause] Below the camera, the California coastline slid away.
outcome: The first stage landed back at Vandenberg, and Sentinel-6 reached orbit in good health.
title: Rocket cam over the California coast
description:
A SpaceX Falcon 9 carrying the U.S.-European Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich ocean satellite launched from Vandenberg Air Force Base, California, on Nov. 21, 2020. The first stage returned for a landing at Vandenberg.

facts.claim: Launched from Vandenberg; first stage landed at VAFB; satellite in orbit and healthy
facts.source_quote: launched to orbit aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket.

extra_sources.excerpt: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, carrying the Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich satellite, launched at 9:17 a.m. PST (12:17 p.m. EST) on Nov. 21, 2020, from Space Launch Complex-4 at Vandenberg Air Force Base (VAFB) in California.

Following launch, the SpaceX Falcon 9 first stage separated and returned to Earth for a vertical landing at VAFB. After arriving in orbit, the Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich satellite separated from the rocket’s second stage and unfolded its twin sets of solar arrays. Ground controllers successfully acquired the satellite’s signal, and initial telemetry reports showed the spacecraft in good health.
